post_title: How many federal units will Fiocruz's InfoGripe SE 44 bulletin (released 12 November 2026) flag with SRAG incidence at alert level or above and a rising long-term trend?

question.title: How many federal units will Fiocruz's InfoGripe SE 44 bulletin (released 12 November 2026) flag with SRAG incidence at alert level or above and a rising long-term trend?
question.description:
InfoGripe is the respiratory-surveillance group of Brazil's Oswaldo Cruz Foundation (Fiocruz). It publishes a Boletim InfoGripe every Thursday, plus a shorter "Resumo" PDF, analysing Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SRAG) notifications entered into the SIVEP-Gripe system up to the Saturday that closes the reference epidemiological week (SE). For each of the 27 federal units (26 states plus the Federal District) and the 27 state capitals, the bulletin reports an activity level based on SRAG incidence over the last two weeks (low/green, alert/yellow, risk/orange, high risk/red) and a trend over the short term (last three weeks) and long term (last six weeks).

The specific metric used here — the number of UFs with SRAG incidence at alert level or above AND a rising long-term trend — has been volatile in recent weeks of the 2026 season:
- SE 39 (data through 3 October): 3 UFs — Alagoas, Roraima, Sergipe.
- SE 40 (data through 10 October, published 15 October): 1 UF — Sergipe; a further 6 UFs (MA, MT, MS, RS, RR, SC) were at alert/risk/high risk but without growth.
- SE 41 (data through 17 October, published 22 October): 3 UFs — Goiás, Mato Grosso, Sergipe.
- SE 42 (data through 24 October, published 29 October): 5 UFs — Amapá, Maranhão, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Sergipe; Roraima and Santa Catarina were at alert/risk/high risk without growth. Nationally, SE 42 reported oscillation/stabilisation in the six-week trend together with an increase in the three-week trend.

In the SE 42 edition, 168,814 SRAG cases had been notified in 2026, of which 90,200 (53.4%) were laboratory-positive, and 7,606 deaths were recorded. Among positive cases in the preceding four weeks, rhinovirus accounted for 53.3%, respiratory syncytial virus 11.5%, SARS-CoV-2 6.4%, influenza A 4.1% and influenza B 5.4%; metapneumovirus was rising in parts of the Centre-South and Northeast (SP, RJ, ES, MS, PR, AL, BA, PE, SE). Brazilian spring (October–November) is normally a period of comparatively low influenza activity, but rhinovirus/enterovirus and metapneumovirus circulation can push local SRAG incidence into alert territory, so the count can move in either direction from one week to the next.

The SE 43 edition, published on Thursday 5 November 2026 (data through 31 October), will already be public before this question opens and is the most recent information available to forecasters. This question concerns the following edition, SE 44 (data through 7 November 2026), expected on Thursday 12 November 2026.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the "Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe – Semana Epidemiológica (SE) 44 2026" published by Fiocruz, expected at https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf ; a version of that file with a filename suffix (e.g. Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44_0.pdf) counts as the same document. The resolved value is the number of Brazilian federal units (26 states plus the Federal District, out of 27 total) that this edition reports as having SRAG incidence at alert level, risk level, or high risk (based on the last two weeks) together with a rising long-term trend (last six weeks) — the figure given in the edition's national-situation bullet of the form "N das 27 unidades federativas apresentam incidência de SRAG em nível de alerta ou risco (últimas duas semanas) com sinal de crescimento na tendência de longo prazo (últimas 6 semanas) até a semana 44", followed by the names of those units. If the edition lists the qualifying units without stating a total, count the distinct units listed; if a stated total and the number of units named disagree, the stated total prevails. If the SE 44 summary is not hosted at that URL or a suffixed variant, the same document published elsewhere on agencia.fiocruz.br or fiocruz.br, or Fiocruz's own press release reporting the SE 44 figure, may be used; failing that, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used. If publication of the SE 44 edition is delayed beyond 13 November 2026, the question resolves on that edition once it is published.
question.fine_print: A "federal unit" (unidade federativa, UF) means one of Brazil's 26 states or the Federal District. A UF counts as "at alert level or above" if the bulletin classifies its SRAG incidence over the last two weeks as "nível de alerta", "nível de risco", or "alto risco" (any level above the low/green baseline). If Fiocruz publishes a corrected version of the SE 44 summary before 23:59 UTC on 13 November 2026, the corrected version is used.
